brief.t: As of 2026-10-09, old-crop (2026/27) unfixed call **sales** are 68.1k contracts (+238 w/w, -1,653 over 8 weeks) and old-crop unfixed **purchases** 29.9k (-729 w/w). Against the same week of the last five seasons, sales are at the 40th percentile (avg 78.9k) and purchases at the 40th (avg 40.4k). Beyond this season, merchants hold 9.7k of new-crop sales and 31.8k of new-crop purchases.

Old-crop unfixed sales are 0.58× the PMU gross long of 117.5k (COT 2026-10-06): **mills hold substantial futures cover, so much of the fixing can move by EFP rather than fresh buying**. Total unfixed purchases of 61.7k (-10,696 over 8 weeks) compare with 255.5k PMU shorts and 29.2k swap-dealer shorts — producer fixing is latent selling, whether it runs through PMU hedges or swap structures.

Front contract **December 2026** is 6.6 weeks from first notice, with 18.4k unfixed sales and 20.4k unfixed purchases against 170.4k open interest. Next: March 2027 with 22.9k unfixed sales. The Dec/Mar spread is -3.26¢, -0.17¢ on the week.

Old-crop unfixed sales of 7.09m bales equal 16% of USDA's 2026/27 world trade forecast (44.7m, October 2026). USDA sees Brazil exporting 16.0m bales vs the US 12.3m. US export sales (week of 2026-10-01): 4.14m running bales unshipped, China 6%.
Managed money is net long 63.8k (-10,756 w/w; 3-yr COT index 77). Spec length is high alongside covered mills, leaving less fresh buying from either side.
